answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The comet multiplier is published, charged in trellis, and whisper lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2727 identities would post 2505 proofs and burn roughly 30 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
